topProblems.problem: On most real laptop screens the product gallery does not pin. It falls back to a rail of cards taller than the screen, so mouse users scroll vertically past it. This is the client's complaint that each product scrolls vertically.
topProblems.evidence: Rail mode at 1366x657, 1536x730, 1280x720, 1280x601, 1024x768 and 1024x600. In each case the card is 665–692px tall against 527–657px available, and the counter and prev/next sit at y 745–838, below the fold. There is no wheel-to-horizontal mapping, so a mouse wheel scrolls the page down past the rail. The neighbour card shows full-contrast text clipped mid-word ('AI-native process managem'). Screenshots: 1366x657-03-gallery.png, 1280x601-03-gallery.png, 1536x730-04-gallery-card2.png.
topProblems.rootCause: lib/breakpoints.ts sets PIN_MIN_HEIGHT = 760, and MQ.pinned requires min-height:760px plus min-width:1280px. Typical laptop inner heights (601–730px) fail that check. In rail mode, showcase.css sets .showcase.is-rail .sc-card{height:100%}, which is effectively the intrinsic height with no viewport cap. --cw:min(88vw,1120px) is left-padded by the gutter, so the first card is not centred and the neighbour is half-visible. In Showcase.tsx, .sc-controls render after the track, below the card.
topProblems.fix: 1) Pin on any width of 1024px or more with a fine pointer and motion allowed, and lower the height gate to about 560px. 2) Size the stage from the viewport: .sc-card{height:clamp(440px, calc(100svh - var(--header-h) - 104px), 720px)}. Give .sc-card container-type:size and add @container (max-height:600px) rules that hide .sc-caps, line-clamp .sc-line to 2 lines and step .sc-name down to 2rem, so content never overflows. 3) Put the counter and arrows inside the 100svh stage, overlaid at the bottom of the card or at its top-right, never after the track. 4) Rail mode is for touch or reduced motion only: centre the first card (padding-inline:calc((100vw - var(--cw))/2)) and dim and scale non-current cards (opacity .3, scale .92) so neighbours read as a peek, not cropped text. 5) Optionally map vertical wheel to horizontal scroll while the rail is centred in view.

topProblems.problem: At short heights the hero does not fit the screen. The CTA buttons are cut or below the fold at 1280x601 and 1024x600, and the hero is taller than the screen at 1366x657.
topProblems.evidence: 1280x601: the CTA bottom is at 643, a 42px gap, and the hero is 675px tall (01-hero.png shows only the top edge of the buttons). 1366x657: the hero is 675px on a 657px viewport and the CTA is 14px from the fold. 1024x600: the CTA is 57px below the fold, with nothing visual above it.
topProblems.rootCause: hero.css changes size in fixed steps: (min-height:860px) sets a 96px H1 and (max-height:800px) sets 64px with 92/32 padding. Below 800px tall there is no further step, so the stack (3-line 64px H1, 2-line lede, 77px moments row, 48px CTA) is always about 550px plus 124px of padding, roughly 675px. The later @media (max-width:1279px) block resets .hero{padding-block:128px 64px; min-height:0}, overriding the short-height compaction at 1024–1279px.
topProblems.fix: Replace the step queries with height-aware fluid values: .hero-title{font-size:clamp(2.25rem, min(6vw, 9.2svh), 6rem)}; .hero-lede/.moments/.hero-cta margins clamp(10px, 2.2svh, 32px); .hero{padding-block:calc(var(--header-h) + 1.5svh) 2.5svh; min-height:100svh; max-height:none}. Add @media (max-height:680px){.moments a{padding-block:8px} .hero-eyebrow{display:none}}. Combine the short-height and narrow-width rules (max-width:1279px) and (max-height:800px) so source order no longer silently wins. Add a Playwright assertion that .hero-cta bottom <= innerHeight at 1280x600, 1366x657 and 1024x600.

topProblems.problem: The 3D room is pushed off the right edge and cropped at every desktop size, which leaves a dead band in the middle of the hero. There is no real foreground/background composition.
topProblems.evidence: Every WebGL viewport (1280–1920 wide): the Command Center panel and far Alerts panel are cut by the viewport's right edge, and the room occupies only about the right 28% of the screen, low. At 1366x657 the panels sit at x 970–1366 and x 830–970 is empty. At 1920x1080 the copy ends at x 1104 and the first panel starts at about x 1300. The room never overlaps the copy: the busy-pixel check behind the H1, lede and moments was 0.000 everywhere. Screenshots: 1366x657-01b-hero-nocopy.png, 1920x1080-01-hero.png, 1536x864-01-hero.png.
topProblems.rootCause: hero.css sets .hero-room{inset:0 -22% 0 var(--room-left:60%)}, so the canvas is 62% of the viewport wide but only 40% is visible, and the left 16% of that is masked out. In room-layout.ts, LOOK_AT [11.6,0.6,-5] projects to the canvas centre, which is about 60%+31% = 91% of the viewport width, so half the scene is outside the screen. The camera has a fixed fov of 42 and z 24, with no aspect-based framing, so panels are small and their crop changes with the aspect ratio. The copy sits in a centred 1280px container while the room is anchored to the viewport edge, so the two halves never share a grid on wide screens.
topProblems.files: app/hero.css (.hero-room, .hero::before); components/room/room-layout.ts (LOOK_AT, CAMERA_POS, ROWS x offsets); components/room/Room.tsx (camera setup)
topProblems.fix: Make the canvas fully visible: .hero-room{inset:0 0 0 max(46%, calc((100vw - var(--content-max))/2 + var(--content-max)*0.5))} with no negative right inset, and shorten the mask to about 8%. In Room.tsx, fit the camera to the PANELS bounding box each time the canvas resizes: read size from useThree(), compute the distance at which the bbox fills about 88% of the canvas, and set LOOK_AT to the bbox centre (about x 11, y 1). That keeps every panel inside the frame at any aspect and makes near panels about 380–450px wide at 1366. For the requested separation into layers, move the scene's background into its own plane (lattice/fog plane at z -30 with slow parallax), keep the panels as the midground with per-row parallax on pointer and scroll, and keep the copy as the foreground with the scrim tightened to its column.

topProblems.problem: At 1024–1279px wide (iPad landscape, 1280px laptops at 125%) the hero has no visual above the fold. It is text on navy, with a single poster stacked below the CTAs.
topProblems.evidence: 1024x768: the poster starts at y 705, so only a 60px sliver of 'Fire & smoke' peeks out (1024x768-01-hero.png). 1024x600: nothing visual is visible and the CTA is hidden. The moments row stretches to 942px for four short labels.
topProblems.rootCause: RoomClient.tsx renders RoomPoster whenever MQ.xl (1280px or wider) fails. hero.css @media (max-width:1279px) switches .hero to a flex column with .hero-room order:2 below the copy and drops the scrim and side-by-side layout. .hero-copy-inner{max-width:none} lets the moments row span the full container.
topProblems.fix: Use a two-column hero from 1024px: grid-template-columns 6fr 6fr, copy left, visual right, visual max-height 62svh. Show the static depth collage (RoomFallback, CSS scale, blur and shadow per depth band) at 1024–1279, not the single poster, and keep the poster only below 768px. Keep .hero-copy-inner{max-width:46rem} at all widths so .moments stays compact.

topProblems.problem: On phones and tablets each product card is a tall vertical document inside a horizontal rail. The media sits at the bottom, below the fold, the arrows are below the card, and the next card barely peeks out.
topProblems.evidence: Card heights against available space: 904/771 (390x844), 907/667 (360x740), 922/823 (414x896), 1077/951 (768x1024), 1117/1107 (820x1180). The media starts at y 678–703 on phones. The next-card peek is about 24–30px. The swipe hint mentions arrows that are about 900px further down. Screenshots: 390x844-03-gallery.png, 820x1180-03-gallery.png.
topProblems.rootCause: showcase.css @media (max-width:1023px) sets .showcase.is-rail .sc-card{grid-template-columns:1fr; align-content:start} with DOM order copy then ScreenFrame, and no height cap. --cw:88vw leaves almost no peek. .sc-controls come after the track in Showcase.tsx.
topProblems.fix: Below 1024px: put the media first (.sc-shot{order:-1; max-height:32svh} with object-fit:contain) and cap the card at height:calc(100svh - var(--header-h) - 112px). Clamp the copy (.sc-line line-clamp 3, show only the first 2 caps, keep the Deploys row). Set --cw:84vw with centred padding so about 8vw of the neighbour shows, scaled to .94 and dimmed. Move the counter and arrows between the heading and the track, or overlay them on the card's bottom edge, so they are always on screen with the card.

topProblems.problem: 'How it works' opens on an empty right column, and its timeline nodes drift away from their step labels on taller screens.
topProblems.evidence: At every viewport of 1024px or wider, the first view of #how shows the heading and steps 01–02 on the left and an empty lattice of about 630x400px on the right (1366x657-05-how.png, 1024x768-05-how.png). The active diamond sits about 40px above its label at 1366x657 and about 116px above it at 1920x1080 (1920x1080-05-how.png).
topProblems.rootCause: In Scenario.tsx, SHOWN[0] resolves to -1 because SCENARIO[0] has no screen, so the sticky media column is empty for step 01. In sections.css, .how-step{min-height:30svh; align-content:center} vertically centres the text while .how-node is positioned at top:4px of the step box.
topProblems.fix: Give step 01 a real, evidenced visual, such as the existing Yisbir fire-and-smoke still shown before its detection overlay, labelled 'Design concept · sample data'. Alternatively show the step-02 screen from the start, dimmed. Change .how-step to align-content:start with padding-block:8svh and align .how-node to the label row (top:calc(8svh + 4px)) so the diamond always marks its title.

topProblems.problem: Pinned mode (1280px or wider and at least 760px tall) works, but it looks flat and leaves dead zones. The cards are single flat surfaces, and the neighbours' text stays readable and noisy.
topProblems.evidence: At 1920x1080 the card is capped at 700px, with 190px empty above it and about 115px below before the controls (1920x1080-03-gallery.png). An empty band of about 150px separates the section heading from the card when the pin starts (1920x937-02-gallery-head.png). Neighbours at 0.35 opacity still show readable, cropped headings ('Tas', 'Tasree3').
topProblems.rootCause: showcase.css .showcase.is-pinned .sc-card{height:min(74svh,700px)} is centred inside .sc-pin{height:100svh; justify-content:center}. .sc-head sits outside the pin with padding-block 64/24. The only state change between cards is opacity on .sc-panel; there are no depth layers in .sc-card.
topProblems.fix: Size the card to the stage, height:min(calc(100svh - var(--header-h) - 112px), 760px), aligned to the top of the stage under the header, and move the section heading into the pinned stage as a small overline. Build the depth the client asked for: a back plate (accent glow and lattice, moving at 0.3x the track speed), a mid layer (the card surface) and a front layer (the media lifted with translateZ or a shadow, moving at 1.15x, its caption offset). Animate them with separate GSAP timelines in the existing scrub. Treat non-current cards with scale .9, blur 2px and opacity .25 so they read as depth rather than cropped text.
